title: Chat Completions API
summary: Chat Completions takes an array of role-tagged messages, returns choices, and keeps no state: your application sends the full history on every call.
useIf: You target many OpenAI-compatible vendors, run non-reasoning models, or want to own conversation state.
avoidIf: You need reasoning models with tools on recent OpenAI models, built-in tools or server-held state. Use the Responses API.

explain.md: A **Chat Completions** request carries a `model` and a `messages` array. Each message has a role such as `system`, `user`, `assistant` or `tool`. The response holds one or more `choices`. The API is **stateless**: nothing is remembered between calls, so your code resends the system prompt and the conversation each time and decides what to trim. OpenAI says Chat Completions stays supported while Responses is recommended for all new projects [[r6]].

explain.md: Chat completions are stored by default for new accounts, and `store: false` turns that off. The endpoint `/v1/chat/completions` is eligible for zero data retention [[r10]]. Limits on newer models: from GPT-5.4 tool calling is not supported with `reasoning_effort` other than `none`, GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol need Responses for tools, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna allow function calling in Chat only with `none` [[r6]] [[r2]].

explain.title: Why portability matters
explain.md: Many vendors implement a Chat-style API, and the Azure v1 API also routes chat completions calls to other providers such as DeepSeek and Grok [[r14]]. Anthropic's OpenAI compatibility layer silently ignores several controls and is for testing, not production [[r36]].

pitfalls.cause: The full history is resent every turn
pitfalls.fix: Trim or summarise old turns, keep a stable prefix for caching and cap tool output sizes

scenarios.title: One endpoint, four providers
scenarios.situation: A platform team exposes one internal chat endpoint that routes to OpenAI, Azure and two open-weight hosts. Models are non-reasoning and applications keep their own history.
unknowns: Which controls do all providers honour?
Do any apps need built-in tools?
scenarios.question: Which interface do you standardise on?

options.name: Route Claude traffic through Anthropic's OpenAI compatibility layer in production
options.why: The layer ignores `seed`, penalties, `logit_bias`, `response_format` and more, and Anthropic says it is for testing.
options.tradeoff: Fine in a test harness to compare outputs quickly.

options.name: A Chat-style message interface at the gateway, with per-vendor adapters and a documented list of controls that are honoured
options.why: Every vendor supports a message list, and adapters hide differences while the control list sets expectations.
options.tradeoff: You maintain adapters and some features, such as server state, stay out of reach.

options.name: Responses everywhere
options.why: Richer features on OpenAI and Azure.
options.tradeoff: Other vendors may lack the API, so the gateway ends up translating anyway.

flips.then: Standardise on Responses and use its built-in tools.

flips.if: A team needs reasoning with tools on GPT-6
flips.then: Give that route a Responses adapter.

scenarios.takeaway: Standardise on the common denominator and isolate platform features behind adapters.

scenarios.title: A 40-turn support chat that keeps getting dearer
scenarios.situation: A support chat averages 40 turns. Cost per conversation grows faster than linearly and late turns feel slower.
constraints: Quality must hold on late turns
unknowns: Which turns carry facts that must stay verbatim?
How large are tool outputs in the history?
scenarios.question: What do you change?

options.name: Move to `previous_response_id` expecting a lower bill
options.why: Chained calls bill all earlier input tokens again, so cost does not fall.
options.tradeoff: Chaining saves code and state handling, not tokens.

options.name: Summarise old turns with a cheap model call and keep recent turns verbatim
options.tradeoff: Summaries are lossy and add a call.

options.name: Keep a stable prefix for caching, trim stale turns, cap tool outputs and keep key facts in a pinned note
options.why: It cuts tokens, keeps the cache prefix intact and preserves the facts that matter.
options.tradeoff: Needs rules for what is pinned and what is trimmed.

flips.if: Conversations must be audited in full
flips.then: Store the full history outside the prompt and send only the trimmed view.

flips.if: You adopt a reasoning model with tools
flips.then: Move to Responses and use compaction where available.

scenarios.takeaway: In a stateless API the history is your cost, so manage it deliberately.

quiz.q: What does 'stateless' mean for Chat Completions?
options: Your application sends the history on every call
The API stores the conversation for 30 days and replays it
The model has no memory of its training data
quiz.explain: The API keeps no conversation state between calls, so your code resends what the model should see. Storage of completions is a separate setting.

quiz.q: Which are true about Chat Completions on newer OpenAI models?
options: Tools with `reasoning_effort` other than `none` are not supported from GPT-5.4
GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol need Responses for tools
`max_tokens` is the recommended cap on o-series
The endpoint is eligible for ZDR
quiz.explain: Tools with reasoning need Responses from GPT-5.4, and GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol need Responses for tools. `max_tokens` is deprecated for o-series. `/v1/chat/completions` is ZDR eligible.

quiz.q: Which need is the strongest reason to stay on Chat Completions?
options: Reasoning with tools on GPT-6 Astra
Targeting several OpenAI-compatible vendors with one format
quiz.explain: Portability is Chat's strength. The other needs favour Responses.

flashcards.front: Why does cost grow over a long Chat Completions conversation?
flashcards.back: The API is stateless, so you resend the full history each turn and pay for those input tokens again.

flashcards.front: Which cap parameter replaces `max_tokens` in Chat Completions?
flashcards.back: `max_completion_tokens`. `max_tokens` is deprecated and not compatible with o-series.

flashcards.front: When must you leave Chat Completions for Responses?
flashcards.back: For reasoning with tools on GPT-5.4 and later, for GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol tools, and for built-in tools or server-held state.
